title: Practice Data Import CSV templates and column reference

claims.claim: The Practice Onboarding importer is at /administrator/practice-onboarding (Practice Onboarding in the Administrator area).
Every column name, required flag, accepted value, validation rule, and fallback default below matches the live importer and downloadable CSV templates.
claims.finding: Several rows below do not match the importer (see cr-f04 to cr-f18 and cr-x claims in this file).

claims.claim: Download the latest template from each step's Upload screen. Templates include a UTF-8 byte-order mark (BOM) and a leading sep=, hint line; the importer strips sep=, automatically when you upload the file back.

claims.claim: Templates overview: 1 Patients (patient_import_template.csv, produces patient_uid); 2 Insurance, 3 Medications, 4 Allergies, 5 Comorbidities, 6 Emergency Contacts, 7 Wounds (produces wound_uid) — each needs Step 1; 8 Documents & Historical Wound Photos needs Step 1 (optional wound_uid from Step 7); 9 Visit History needs Step 7; all nine Active.
The Patients template contains 22 columns: 11 core demographic and provider fields (3 required, 8 optional), 3 optional identity and duplicate-handling fields, and 8 optional consent_* fields.
first_name, last_name and date_of_birth are required; date_of_birth must be a valid calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD (recommended) or MM/DD/YYYY; rollover dates such as 2026-02-31 are rejected.

checks.pattern: return 'Date must be YYYY-MM-DD or MM/DD/YYYY';

claims.claim: phone, address_street, address_city are optional and stored as null if blank; email is optional and must match name@domain.tld if provided.
address_state is validated against 2-letter US state and territory codes; address_zip must be 5-digit or 9-digit (ZIP+4).

checks.pattern: return 'State must be a valid 2-letter US state code (e.g. IL, TX)';

claims.claim: provider_email: if matched to an existing provider, assigns the provider and sets patient status to ASSIGNED; blank or unmatched imports the patient unassigned (status NEW) with a Needs Follow-Up warning.
notes: free-text note saved to the patient's notes with note_date = import date.
prior_ehr_system: name of the source EHR.
prior_ehr_system namespaces prior_ehr_mrn in patient.external_id as <prior_ehr_system>:<mrn> (lowercased, colons removed).
claims.finding: Internal storage detail; the stated format was not confirmed in patientIdentity.ts.

claims.claim: prior_ehr_mrn: leading zeros are normalized; a re-import with matching prior_ehr_mrn + first_name + date_of_birth is recognized as the same patient; if prior_ehr_mrn matches an existing patient whose first_name or date_of_birth differs, the row is blocked unless confirmed.

claims.claim: If consent_on_file is blank or no, no consent attestation is created and the other 7 consent_* columns are ignored.

If consent_on_file contains an unrecognized value (anything other than yes/no, true/false, 1/0, y/n), the patient still imports, no consent is recorded, and a non-blocking warning is added to the Needs Follow-Up list.
claims.finding: An unrecognized value is treated as no with no warning (functions/practice-onboarding-import/consentAttest.ts:28).
claims.proposed_text: consent_on_file: only yes, true, 1 or y records a consent; blank, no or anything else records nothing, and the other 7 columns are ignored.

claims.claim: Setting consent_on_file = yes records an externally attested, current consent to treatment and to bill, attested under the signed-in administrator's account.

Only set consent_on_file = yes when your practice holds its own signed consent; never use a skilled nursing facility's admission paperwork or list facility staff as the signer — facility staff cannot legally consent on a resident's behalf.
If a patient already has a current consent, re-importing with consent_on_file = yes leaves it untouched and logs a non-blocking warning.

checks.pattern: message: 'a consent is already on file for this patient; left as it is'

claims.claim: Internal storage names: consent_location is stored in external_document_location, consent_witnessed in external_witnessed, consent_photo in consent_to_photo, consent_npp_acknowledged in npp_acknowledged; medications and allergies are created with source = 'imported'.
claims.finding: The fields are external_location, external_was_witnessed, photo_consent and hipaa_acknowledged (functions/practice-onboarding-import/consentAttest.ts:56); imported rows carry source = 'practice_onboarding' (patientIdentity.ts IMPORT_SOURCE).
claims.proposed_text: (remove the internal field names; keep the behaviour described)

claims.claim: consent_signed_on: stored in external_signed_on and sets signed_at to YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00Z; if blank or unreadable, signed_at defaults to the import timestamp; an unreadable date logs a warning on the Confirm screen.
claims.finding: An unreadable date is silently dropped (functions/practice-onboarding-import/consentAttest.ts:38); the column is plain text, so no Confirm-screen warning appears.
claims.proposed_text: consent_signed_on: YYYY-MM-DD or MM/DD/YYYY; an unreadable date is dropped, never guessed.

claims.finding: Unrecognized values default to patient with no warning (functions/practice-onboarding-import/consentAttest.ts:34); writers.ts raises no consent_signer_capacity warning.
claims.proposed_text: consent_signer_capacity: patient, poa or surrogate; blank or any other value is saved as patient.

claims.claim: consent_signer_name defaults to the row's first_name last_name; consent_witnessed yes/no (blank not recorded); consent_location defaults to "practice records (onboarding import)"; consent_photo and consent_npp_acknowledged default to off unless yes.

claims.claim: Immediately after an import finishes, click Download Results CSV on the Results screen to download patients_import_results.csv or wounds_import_results.csv.
Anytime later, completed Step 1 — Patients and Step 7 — Wounds cards display a persistent Download results CSV action, so you can re-download after Done, refreshing, or signing in elsewhere.

patients_import_results.csv columns: csv_row, first_name, last_name, date_of_birth, patient_uid. wounds_import_results.csv columns: csv_row, patient_uid, wound_location, wound_type, first_seen_date, wound_uid.
claims.finding: The immediate download is your uploaded CSV plus the ID column (services/importService.ts:1165); the saved Patients download also has prior_ehr_mrn.
claims.proposed_text: Right after an import, Download Results CSV gives your uploaded CSV with the new ID column added. Later, the completed Patients and Wounds cards have Download results CSV; columns csv_row, first_name, last_name, date_of_birth, prior_ehr_mrn, patient_uid (Patients) and csv_row, patient_uid, wound_location, wound_type, first_seen_date, wound_uid (Wounds).

claims.claim: Re-import matching: Insurance on payer + policy number; Allergies on allergen; Comorbidities merged without repeats; Emergency Contacts on name + phone; Wounds on location, type, first-seen date.
Step 8 (Documents & Historical Wound Photos) deduplicates by SHA-256 content hash.

claims.claim: Medication status: active, discontinued (aliases: stopped, inactive, d/c, dc), or held (aliases: hold, on_hold); defaults to active if blank; unrecognized values default to active with a warning.
claims.finding: The importer also accepts completed and unknown (functions/practice-onboarding-import/writers.ts:970).
claims.proposed_text: Medication status: active, discontinued (stopped, inactive, d/c, dc), held (hold, on_hold), completed or unknown; blank means active; anything else is saved as active with a warning.

claims.claim: Allergies: allergen_name required; allergy_type medication, food, environmental, latex, insect, other, or nkda; defaults to other if blank, other with a warning if unrecognized.

Allergy severity (required): mild (aliases: low, minor), moderate, severe, life_threatening (aliases: life-threatening, life threatening, high, critical, anaphylaxis), or none; if an unrecognized value reaches the backend, it defaults to moderate with a warning.
claims.finding: The Confirm screen accepts only mild, moderate, severe and life_threatening (components/import/modules/AllergiesImportModule.tsx:29); the backend fallback is none, not moderate (functions/practice-onboarding-import/writers.ts:1046).
claims.proposed_text: Allergy severity is required: mild, moderate, severe or life_threatening (life-threatening and life threatening also work); any other value is an error on the Confirm screen.

claims.claim: Comorbidities: patient_uid and condition required; one condition per row; multiple rows for one patient are grouped; duplicate conditions are skipped.
Emergency Contacts: patient_uid and contact_name required; relationship, phone_number, email (name@domain.tld), is_primary optional.
is_primary accepts true/false, yes/no, 1/0 (case-insensitive) and defaults to false if blank.

claims.claim: Imported wounds (Step 8) and visits (Step 9) are stored in read-only history tables; imported history records cannot be edited, signed, or billed as active Medipyxis visits, and wound photos are not migrated.
claims.finding: Historical wound photos are migrated in Step 8 (mediaImport.ts appends to wound_import_history.photo_urls); wounds are Step 7, not Step 8.

Step 7 produces wound_uid in wounds_import_results.csv so Step 8 and Step 9 can link to historical wounds.

Wounds: patient_uid and wound_location required; wound_type, wound_etiology, wound_status (defaults to active), length_cm, width_cm, depth_cm, first_seen_date, prior_treatments and diagnosis_codes (split on , or ; into a list), notes (saved to treatment_notes) optional.
